messages.text: Nicholls breaks record for Jumps wins with Warwick triumph

metadata.summary: Paul Nicholls reflected on a “fantastic journey” after rewriting the record books by surpassing Martin Pipe’s all-time National Hunt tally for winners by a British trainer.
metadata.content: Paul Nicholls breaks record for National Hunt wins after surpassing Martin Pipe’s all-time tally with Warwick triumph | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Paul Nicholls breaks record for National Hunt wins after surpassing Martin Pipe’s all-time tally with Warwick triumph Ditcheat handler Paul Nicholls became the winning-most trainer in British National Hunt history, surpassing the great Martin Pipe's total of 3,390 when Knappers Hill crossed the line in front at Lingfield, donning the colours of Paul Barber Thursday 19 November 2026 14:19, UK Image: Paul Nicholls has trained more National Hunt winners than any other handler Paul Nicholls reflected on a “fantastic journey” after rewriting the record books by surpassing Martin Pipe’s all-time National Hunt tally for winners by a British trainer. The 14-time champion eclipsed Pipe's record of 3,930 wins at Warwick on Thursday after Knappers Hill toughed out victory in the Denis O'Connell Memorial Veterans' Handicap Chase under Sam Twiston-Davies, carrying the colours of the trainer's long-time friend and mentor Paul Barber. Nicholls, who has been training at Manor Farm Stables in Somerset since 1991 after first renting the yard from Barber, was thrilled to etch his name into the history of a sport in which he has long been a master of his craft. metadata.summary: Will Joseph has retained his place on the wing for England's Nations Championship Test against New Zealand on Saturday, with Fin Smith among those restored and Henry Pollock dropped to the bench.
metadata.content: Nations Championship: Will Joseph retains England place vs New Zealand's All Blacks as Henry Pollock dropped amid nine changes | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nations Championship: Will Joseph retains England place vs New Zealand's All Blacks as Henry Pollock dropped amid nine changes Steve Borthwick makes nine changes to England XV for visit of All Blacks in Nations Championship on Saturday (2.10pm); Fin Smith, George Furbank, Tommy Freeman, Seb Atkinson, Jamie George, Fin Baxter, Joe Heyes, Ollie Chessum, Ben Curry all return; Will Joseph keeps place on wing Thursday 19 November 2026 14:00, UK Image: Will Joseph has retained his place in England's starting XV to face the All Blacks on Saturday Will Joseph has retained his place on the wing for England's Nations Championship Test against New Zealand on Saturday, with Fin Smith among those restored and Henry Pollock dropped to the bench. Joseph, who missed out on a place in England's matchday 23 for their 45-22 defeat of Australia a fortnight ago , started in last week's crushing 78-15 success over Japan, scoring five tries. The 24-year-old picked up just his second Test cap in that victory at Twickenham, and his first since July 2022 under Eddie Jones. He moves from right to left wing for the visit of the All Blacks. metadata.summary: Andy Farrell has named Dan Sheehan out of position at No 8 for Ireland's crunch Nations Championship Test against South Africa in Dublin on Saturday.
metadata.content: Nations Championship: Dan Sheehan starts at No 8 for Ireland vs South Africa and Sam Prendergast plays after avoiding ban | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nations Championship: Dan Sheehan starts at No 8 for Ireland vs South Africa and Sam Prendergast plays after avoiding ban Ireland hooker and captain Dan Sheehan has been shifted out of position to start at No 8 for the visit of South Africa to Dublin in Saturday's Nations Championship (4.40pm) in unusual and risky Andy Farrell move; Fly-half Sam Prendergast starts after citing against him dismissed Thursday 19 November 2026 14:08, UK Image: Dan Sheehan has been named to start at No 8 for Ireland against South Africa Andy Farrell has named Dan Sheehan out of position at No 8 for Ireland's crunch Nations Championship Test against South Africa in Dublin on Saturday. The unusual move, with Sheehan's ordinary position at hooker, comes with Ireland missing trio Caelan Doris, Jack Conan and Sean Jansen due to injury. Sheehan has only played at No 8 once in his career to date, starting there for Leinster against Munster in last month's URC contest at the Aviva Stadium - a clash in which Leinster badly lost the breakdown battle before coming through to win. Other changes see full-back Hugo Keenan, centre Robbie Henshaw and lock Joe McCarthy return to the squad to start. messages.text: Harmer stars as South Africa beat Bangladesh

metadata.summary: Simon Harmer ran through Bangladesh's tail and South Africa knocked off the 12 runs required to win the first Test by nine wickets on Thursday, taking a 1-0 lead in the teams' two-match series.
metadata.content: South Africa vs Bangladesh: Simon Harmer stars as Proteas seal nine-wicket first Test win | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content South Africa vs Bangladesh: Simon Harmer stars as Proteas seal nine-wicket first Test win South Africa edged closer to securing a spot in the World Test Championship final with a nine-wicket victory against Bangladesh on Thursday; Simon Harmer took four wickets to bowl out Bangladesh; watch the second Test live on Sky Sports Cricket Thursday 19 November 2026 12:19, UK Image: Simon Harmer starred as South Africa wrapped up a nine-wicket win againt Bangladesh Simon Harmer ran through Bangladesh's tail and South Africa knocked off the 12 runs required to win the first Test by nine wickets on Thursday, taking a 1-0 lead in the teams' two-match series. The win sees the Proteas edge closer to securing a spot at the World Test Championship final at The Kia Oval in 2027, with the defending champions having dethroned Australia to go top of the ICC rankings following their series win last month. Resuming on 100-5 at the Wanderers, Bangladesh's lower-order batters couldn't handle the off-spin of Harmer, who took four of the remaining five wickets to help dismiss the tourists for 168 and return figures of 6-51. messages.text: Joshua unable to see new baby daughter until after Fury fight

metadata.summary: Anthony Joshua became a father for the second time after the birth of a daughter last weekend, although ongoing training for his fight against Tyson Fury means he is not able to see her until mid-December.
metadata.content: Anthony Joshua: British heavyweight boxer becomes dad for second time but unable to see daughter until after Tyson Fury fight | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Anthony Joshua: British heavyweight boxer becomes dad for second time but unable to see daughter until after Tyson Fury fight Anthony Joshua says ongoing training camp for his fight against Tyson Fury on December 11 means he will not see his new-born daughter until the days after the fight; "It's not ideal but she is in good hands", says Joshua, who describes daughter's arrival as a "big blessing" Thursday 19 November 2026 11:17, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Joshua made his predictions for his fight against Tyson Fury on December 11 Anthony Joshua became a father for the second time after the birth of a daughter last weekend, although ongoing training for his fight against Tyson Fury means he is not able to see her until mid-December. Joshua, whose son JJ was born in 2015, is currently in training camp in Marbella in preparation for his blockbuster all-British fight against Fury on December 11 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium, and was unable to be at the birth. Joshua says the arrival of his daughter, who has not yet been named, is "amazing" and "a big blessing" as the 37-year-old paid tribute to Nicole, the mother of both children.
